tags.name: Audit logs
tags.description: Audit logs are used to track end-user activities in Logto sign-in experience and other flows. It does not include activities in Logto Console.

get.description:
Get logs that match the given query with pagination.

### Pagination on large result sets

For tenants with very large log volumes, the default exact `count(*)` may exceed Postgres `statement_timeout`. Pass `enableCap=true` to short-circuit the count query: any tenant with more than 10,000 matching logs saturates `Total-Number` at the sentinel value `10001` and the response includes `Total-Number-Is-Capped: true`. In capped responses the `Link` header omits `rel="last"` and `rel="next"`; walk forward by incrementing `page` and stop on an empty response.

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on `createdAt`, in unix milliseconds. When set, returns only logs where `createdAt >= start_time`. Recommended for clients paginating across very large log ranges to keep query latency consistent. Because the bound is inclusive, when resuming pagination from the last fetched log, pass its `createdAt + 1` as `start_time` (or de-duplicate by log `id`) to avoid re-fetching the boundary log.

parameters.name: end_time
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on `createdAt`, in unix milliseconds. When set, returns only logs where `createdAt <= end_time`. Returns `400` if `start_time > end_time` when both are present.

parameters.name: enableCap
parameters.description: When `true`, short-circuits the underlying `count(*)` query: any tenant with more than 10,000 matching logs saturates `Total-Number` at the sentinel value `10001` and the response emits `Total-Number-Is-Capped: true`. The `Link` header then omits `rel="last"` and `rel="next"` because the real total is unknown. Default `false`; recommended `true` for any client whose tenant volume may exceed 10,000 matching logs to avoid `statement_timeout`.

400.description: Returned when `start_time` or `end_time` is not a finite number, or when `start_time > end_time`.

200.description: An array of logs that match the given query.

Total-Number.description: When `enableCap=false`: exact match count. When `enableCap=true`: either the exact count (≤ 10,000) or the saturation sentinel `10001`; inspect `Total-Number-Is-Capped` to distinguish.

Total-Number-Is-Capped.description: Present and set to `true` only when `enableCap=true` and the result has more than 10,000 matching logs (in which case `Total-Number` is `10001`). Consumers should treat `Total-Number` as `> 10,000` when this header is present.

Link.description: Pagination links per RFC 5988. `rel="first"` and `rel="prev"` are emitted as usual. When the response is capped (`Total-Number-Is-Capped: true`), `rel="last"` and `rel="next"` are omitted because the saturated count makes the derived page count unreliable — clients should walk forward by incrementing `page` and stop on an empty response.

delete.description:
Delete log rows in bounded batches.

`start_time` / `end_time` carry the same inclusive semantics as `GET /api/logs`: a row is deleted when its `createdAt` falls in `[start_time, end_time]`, at millisecond granularity. Note that this operation removes **every** log row in that window, while `GET /api/logs` returns audit logs only.

Webhook delivery logs (`TriggerHook.*`) share the `logs` table and are included by `GET /api/logs/export` by default; set `excludeWebhookLogs=true` there to leave them out. With that option, `deletedCount` can exceed the number of rows an export returned. A window covering the last 24 hours also removes the deliveries counted by the execution stats on `GET /api/hooks`.

`end_time` is required, so a bare `DELETE /api/logs` never means "delete everything". `end_time` must not be in the future and is rejected with `400` otherwise; a common cause is passing microseconds or nanoseconds instead of milliseconds, or a miscomputed timezone offset. Passing seconds instead yields a boundary in the past, which deletes nothing rather than deleting too much.

This operation is irreversible and reachable by any Management API token. Each call deletes at most `limit` rows in a single statement and reports `hasMore`. Keep both bounds fixed across calls and repeat while `hasMore` is `true`; recomputing a boundary between calls would skip rows. Run one cleanup at a time: a concurrent purge can make `hasMore` under-report.

### Performance

`DELETE` marks rows dead and leaves index cleanup to autovacuum, so writes are dominated by heap tuples and WAL. The statement is matched on `ctid`, so the outer side is a Tid Scan over exactly `limit` rows and the inner select reads those row ids from `logs__created_at_id`; expect the cost of a call to track `limit` rather than the size of the table. Measure with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` on your own data before running a large purge.

Freed space is reused by later inserts but the table file does not shrink, so disk usage will not drop immediately after a purge.

parameters.name: end_time
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on `createdAt`, in unix milliseconds, with the same semantics as `GET /api/logs`. Only log rows with `createdAt <= end_time` are deleted. Returns `400` if the value is in the future.

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on `createdAt`, in unix milliseconds, with the same semantics as `GET /api/logs`. Only log rows with `createdAt >= start_time` are deleted. Omit to purge everything up to `end_time`. Returns `400` if it is after `end_time`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows deleted by this call. Default `1000`, maximum `10000`. Returns `400` for values outside that range.

200.description: Summary of the rows deleted by this call. `deletedCount` is the number of log rows deleted, and `deletedRange` is an optional `{ oldest, newest }` object holding the unix-millisecond timestamps of the deleted rows; it is omitted when nothing was deleted. `hasMore` is `true` when `deletedCount` equals `limit`, meaning this batch was full rather than that more rows definitely exist, so the caller should repeat the request with the same bounds.

400.description: Returned when `end_time` is missing, empty, negative, outside the safe integer range, in the future, or not a finite number; when `start_time` is malformed or after `end_time`; or when `limit` is outside `1..10000`.

get.description:
Export logs as a streamed CSV or JSONL download.

Filters use the same semantics as `GET /api/logs`: `userId`, `applicationId`, `logKey`, and the inclusive `start_time` / `end_time` window in unix milliseconds. By default every matching log row in the window is exported, including webhook delivery logs (`TriggerHook.*`), so an unfiltered export followed by `DELETE /api/logs` is lossless. Set `excludeWebhookLogs=true` to export audit logs only, matching `GET /api/logs`; webhook delivery logs can then be read through `GET /api/hooks/{id}/recent-logs`.

Rows are streamed in ascending `createdAt` order. CSV starts with the header `tenantId,id,key,createdAt,payload`; each payload is a JSON string, and cells containing delimiters, quotes, or line breaks are quoted. JSONL emits one object per line with the same five fields. Both formats are UTF-8 with LF line endings.

Every non-empty export reports the actual range of its rows in the `X-Log-Range-Oldest` and `X-Log-Range-Newest` response headers, in unix milliseconds. The range is measured before streaming starts; with `end_time` in the past and no concurrent writes or deletes, it matches the file. An empty result omits both headers.

`end_time` is required and must not be in the future, so every export has an upper bound. The export is not paginated: one request streams every matching row. It has no `Content-Length` and a mid-stream failure aborts the download instead of appending an error document; discard a truncated file and retry with the same bounds. The pages are not read in a single transaction, so do not delete rows from the same window until the download completes.

### Performance

Rows are read one page at a time with a keyset cursor on `createdAt` and `id`, so memory use tracks the page size rather than the number of rows. The range headers come from one extra descending limit-1 query on the same index. Set `start_time` to keep the scan short; omitting it streams the tenant's entire log history up to `end_time`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Download format. `csv` returns a header row followed by one row per log; `jsonl` returns one JSON object per line.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Filter logs by user ID, with the same semantics as `GET /api/logs`.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Filter logs by application ID, with the same semantics as `GET /api/logs`.

parameters.name: logKey
parameters.description: Filter logs by log key, with the same semantics as `GET /api/logs`.

parameters.name: excludeWebhookLogs
parameters.description: When `true`, export audit logs only and omit webhook delivery logs (`TriggerHook.*`), matching `GET /api/logs`. Default `false`: every log row in the window is exported, including webhook delivery logs.

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on `createdAt`, in unix milliseconds. Omit to export everything up to `end_time`. Returns `400` if it is after `end_time`.

parameters.name: end_time
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on `createdAt`, in unix milliseconds. Only logs with `createdAt <= end_time` are exported. Returns `400` if the value is in the future.

200.description: A streamed export of the matching logs, in ascending `createdAt` order. CSV uses the column order `tenantId,id,key,createdAt,payload`; JSONL emits the same fields as an object on each line. `X-Log-Range-Oldest` and `X-Log-Range-Newest` report the actual unix-millisecond range of the rows in the file and are omitted when nothing matches. Before deleting the exported range, make sure the download completed.

X-Log-Range-Oldest.description: Unix-millisecond `createdAt` of the oldest row in the export. Omitted when no rows match.

X-Log-Range-Newest.description: Unix-millisecond `createdAt` of the newest row in the export. Omitted when no rows match.

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename for the download, ending in `.csv` or `.jsonl`.

Cache-Control.description: Always `no-store`, because the export contains audit data.

400.description: Returned when `format` is missing or not `csv` / `jsonl`; when `excludeWebhookLogs` is not `true` or `false`; when `end_time` is missing, empty, negative, outside the safe integer range, in the future, or not a finite number; or when `start_time` is malformed or after `end_time`.
